issues.body: SV-ND-2 unconditionally says that a request whose bound index is unreadable or absent MUST be indistinguishable from the same request against a non-existent index. SV-ND-4, the following explanation, and the Unreadable descriptor conformance scenario instead permit and require distinguishable results when the requester has at least one eligible entry: neighbours are returned with the unreadable-descriptor bound index, while an unbound service returns zero solutions. Because SV-ND-2 contains no eligible-entry qualification, a conforming implementation cannot satisfy both normative requirements.
issues.fix_hint: Qualify SV-ND-2 itself: bound-index unreadability or absence must be indistinguishable from a non-existent index only when the requester has an empty eligible entry set. Keep seed and referenced-graph unreadability/absence indistinguishable unconditionally. Ensure the nearby explanation and conformance scenario use exactly the same boundary.
issues.title: SV-ND-2 still contradicts the bound-index disclosure exception

verdict.summary: Round 5 remains materially unchanged on the prior major finding. SV-ND-4 and the Unreadable descriptor conformance scenario expressly permit a requester with at least one eligible entry to distinguish a bound index with an unreadable descriptor from no bound index, and to infer its dimension. However, SV-ND-2 still unconditionally requires a request whose bound index is unreadable or absent to be indistinguishable from the same request against a non-existent index. Explanatory prose cannot narrow that normative MUST. The specification therefore continues to prescribe incompatible behavior, so progress is stagnant and approval remains blocked.
